analysis.title: GS - Garrett - 2026 vs 2018 pre-weekend prep - 20 Nov 2026
key_insights: Client conversations are comparing the current market to Q4 2018. The desk cites a hawkish Fed, technical breakdowns, extreme volatility and systematic supply as shared features.
GS tools were used to measure how much of the 2018 drawdown has been realized across asset classes, using the 6-Oct close as the starting point for the 2018 analog.
Equities are close to the 2018 path, especially tech. NDX has realized about 70% of its 2018 drop (-15.1%), SPX 42% (-8.2%) and RTY about a quarter (-6.2%).
If 2018 were to play out from the 6-Oct close, the desk calculates roughly another 12% downside on SPX (to about 6,294), 8% on NDX and 21% on RTY.

Credit is the largest difference from 2018 and has barely moved. CDX IG is +5bp (15% of the 2018 widening) and HY is +38bp (28% of the 2018 +136bp). A 2018 repeat would mean about 27bp more on IG and 98bp more on HY.
Rates have done about half the work. 10y swaps are -23bp (64% of 2018) and 5y swaps are -17bp (42%). 2y swaps are -2bp (7%), so the front end is not pricing a policy response the way it did in 2018.
Copper has realized 2x its 2018 move (-13.1%). Crude is -7.0% against a -41% drop in 2018.
High-beta FX has already exceeded the 2018 move. AUDUSD is at 160% of its 2018 move and USDMXN at 127%. EURUSD is at 85%, USDCHF 59% and USDCAD 17%.
Havens have moved the wrong way. USDJPY is +1.0% while the yen rallied in 2018. Gold is -10.8% against +5.0% in 2018. Neither hedged this time.
Desk anecdote: today is one of the first days offense is being played through equity volatility, but as selling skew (fading the bid to the wings on both sides) rather than buying calls.

sector_views.rationale: The desk says equity damage is clearly concentrated in tech, with NDX at about 70% of its 2018 drawdown versus 42% for SPX. No rating or allocation view is stated.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Long-end rates have moved about two thirds of the way along the 2018 path.
The belly has done less than the 10y.
The front end is not pricing a policy response the way it did in 2018.
Investment grade credit has barely moved relative to 2018.
High yield has widened about a quarter of the 2018 amount.

risk_factors: If 2018 plays out from the 6-Oct close, the desk's math implies about 12% more downside on SPX (to about 6,294), 8% on NDX and 21% on RTY.
Credit has widened far less than in 2018. A catch-up would mean about 27bp more on IG and 98bp more on HY.
Gold and the yen have not provided hedges, unlike in 2018.
The front end is not pricing a policy response, so there is no Fed cushion priced the way there was in 2018.
vol_and_positioning: The desk sees offense being played through equity volatility for one of the first times, by selling skew rather than buying calls. Clients are fading the bid to the wings on both sides.
The desk's 2018 comparison cites extreme volatility and systematic supply as shared features with the current selloff.
